original_value: The wide availability of sensing modules and computing capabilities in modern mobile devices (smartphones, smart watches, in-vehicle sensors, etc.) is driving the shift from mote-class wireless sensor networks (WSNs) to the new era of crowdsensing WSNs. In this emerging paradigm sensors are no longer static and homogeneous, but are rather worn/carried by people or cars. This results in a new type of wide-area WSN—crowd-based and overlaid on top of heterogeneous communication technologies—that paves the way for very innovative applications. To this aim, the positioning of mobile devices operating in the network becomes crucial. Indeed, the pervasive, almost ubiquitous availability of smart devices brings unprecedented opportunities but also poses new research challenges in their precise location under mobility and dense-multipath environments typical of urban and indoor scenarios. In this paper, we review recent advances in the field of wireless positioning with focus on cooperation, mobility, and advanced array processing, which are key enablers for the design of novel localization solutions for crowdsensing WSNs.

result.paraphrase: The widespread presence of sensing modules and computing power in today’s mobile devices—such as smartphones, smart watches, and in-vehicle sensors—is pushing the transition from mote-class wireless sensor networks (WSNs) to crowdsensing WSNs. In this emerging model, sensors are no longer fixed and homogeneous; instead, they are worn or carried by people or cars. This creates a new kind of wide-area WSN, crowd-based and layered over heterogeneous communication technologies, opening the door to highly innovative applications. For this reason, locating mobile devices within the network is essential. The near-ubiquitous availability of smart devices offers unprecedented opportunities, but it also introduces new research challenges in accurately determining their position in mobility and dense-multipath environments typical of urban and indoor settings. In this paper, we review recent progress in wireless positioning, emphasizing cooperation, mobility, and advanced array processing as key enablers for new localization solutions for crowdsensing WSNs.
